hints.content: **Reflective (or line) symmetry** means that we can reflect a figure across a line, and the figure will remain unchanged.

##Reflection over $\overline{AD}$

Under this transformation, each point on the hexagon maps to another point which is also on the hexagon.



[[☃ image 1]]

The hexagon is *symmetric* over this line.

options.alt: An irregular hexagon A B C D E F where every side is congruent. Angles A, C, and E are all congruent obtuse angles, and angles B, D, and F are all congruent acute angles. There is a line segment from point A to point D to reflect the hexagon over. When reflected over this line, the hexagon is mapped onto itself.

hints.content:
##Reflection over $\overline{CE}$

Under this transformation, some points on the hexagon map to another point which is no longer on the hexagon.  



[[☃ image 1]]

The hexagon is *not symmetric* over this line.

options.alt: An irregular hexagon A B C D E F where every side is congruent. Angles A, C, and E are all congruent obtuse angles, and angles B, D, and F are all congruent acute angles. There is a line segment from point C to point E to reflect the hexagon over. When reflected over this line, the hexagon is not mapped onto itself.

hints.content:
The symmetries that apply to the hexagon are:

Symmetry | Applies to the figure?
:- | :-:
Reflective symmetry over $\overline{AD}$ | Yes
Reflective symmetry over $\overline{CE}$ | No
